title: Generator–Validator–Repair (GVR) loop effectiveness using deterministic reachability validation for intent→configuration
research_question: Does an LLM-driven generate–validate–repair (GVR) loop using a deterministic reachability validator increase the rate of correct, safely executable configurations (no unintended reachability changes) versus plain LLM generation on intent→configuration NetOps tasks?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: The paired proportion of intents yielding correct, safely executable configurations (execution-validated) is higher after the GVR loop than for baseline plain-LLM generation (primary confirmatory hypothesis, paired analysis).

H2: Among residual failures after the GVR loop, a plurality are attributable to ambiguous or underspecified natural-language intents (specification ambiguity) rather than validator or execution defects.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How do iteration counts (repairs needed) distribute across intent-complexity strata?
EQ2: What categories of validator–execution discrepancies occur (validator false negatives vs emulation-only failures)?
benchmark_scope: Public NetOps intent→config examples filtered by automated contamination checks (public datasets only)
Synthetic intent templates (deterministic, seed-controlled) to supplement filtered public tasks
Emulated device-level execution using containerized Mininet + containerized router images (Docker)
secondary_estimands: baseline_success_rate (proportion of intents with execution-validated correct configs for baseline)
validator–execution discrepancy rate (proportion of intents where validator passed but execution shows unintended reachability change)
sampling_plan: Automated procedure: 1) harvest candidate intent→config pairs from publicly available NetOps corpora and public config repositories; 2) run deterministic provenance/contamination checks (exact-string, k=8-token shingle Jaccard, token-overlap thresholds) and exclude candidates flagged above thresholds; 3) supplement with deterministically seeded synthetic intent templates to reach N=300; 4) stratify tasks by intent complexity (simple/medium/complex) via deterministic token/AST heuristic; 5) draw final 300 preserving strata proportions using preregistered fixed RNG seed. Inclusion: tasks passing contamination and syntactic-validity checks. Exclusion: contamination-flagged items and irrecoverable technical-retrieval failures (logged). All selection automated.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: 10 percentage-point absolute increase. Method: McNemar-style paired-proportion normal-approximation using assumed discordant-pair fraction 0.35, two-sided alpha=0.05, power=0.80. Recommended N=300 (see preregistration power_plan sensitivity analyses). Report paired difference, 95% CI, p-value; include sensitivity recomputations for discordant fractions 0.25 and 0.45 and a sensitivity treating excluded pairs as failures.
exclusion_rules: Exclude tasks flagged by deterministic contamination heuristics (exact-string match >=95% or shingle Jaccard >=0.6).
Exclude items failing deterministic syntactic validation or parser round-trip irrecoverably.

Pairs where both baseline and guarded execution traces cannot be produced due to technical infrastructure failure after allowed retries are excluded under primary analysis ('complete_pair_primary') and reported in counts.
missingness_plan: Primary analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary'—exclude pairs with technical infrastructure failures preventing both baseline and guarded traces. Log all such pairs and report counts. Sensitivity analysis treats excluded pairs as failures ('complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'). Retry policy: up to 2 automated retries for transient API/container startup failures with exponential backoff; after retries, log as technical failure.
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory analysis executed by registered executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' with estimand 'paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline'. Unit = intent (paired baseline vs guarded). Outcome per pair: 1 if execution-validated config satisfies intent and shows no unintended reachability changes, else 0. Primary test: two-sided paired-proportion (McNemar-style approximation), alpha=0.05. Report paired difference, 95% CI, p-value. Prespecified failed_call_treatment: 'complete_pair_primary' with sensitivity 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'. Secondary/exploratory analyses: descriptive failure-mode breakdowns, repair-iteration histograms, validator–execution discrepancy contingency tables; exploratory p-values corrected with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR; exploratory results not elevated to confirmatory claims.
multiplicity_plan: One pre-registered primary paired test. All subgroup and secondary comparisons are exploratory and reported with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction; exploratory findings are explicitly labeled and not treated as confirmatory.
stopping_rule: Process the full preregistered task_count (N=300). Stop early only if the maximum_model_calls budget (600 calls) is exhausted or the 7-day wall-clock execution budget is reached; in those early-stop cases record partial-completion metadata and treat analysis as prespecified (report observed N and run sensitivity analyses). Retry policy: up to 2 automated retries per transient failure; after retries, log as technical failure and follow missingness_plan.
planned_outputs: IEEE-format short paper (≤5 pages) including mandatory Disclosure Statement
Code and Docker images for validator and emulation; model prompt templates; raw model-call logs and hashes
